title: Space Allocation Criteria for Heavy Vehicle Parking Lots for Each Town
what_it_is: Space Allocation Criteria for Heavy Vehicle Parking Lots for Each Town

sections.label: Heavy vehicle parking lots islandwide
sections.summary: As of December 2021, about 42,100 heavy vehicle lots and 32,400 registered heavy vehicles mean sufficient lots islandwide, though residential-area parking has high opportunity cost.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: As of December 2021, there are about 42,100 Heavy Vehicle (HV) lots islandwide, and about 32,400 HVs registered under LTA's Vehicle Parking Certificate (VPC) scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Hence, there are sufficient lots for all HVs islandwide.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: We recognise that some HV drivers may prefer to park near where they reside.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: However, locating HV parks (HVPs) in or near residential areas comes at a high opportunity cost, as the land could otherwise cater to housing or other community needs.

sections.label: Reducing public heavy vehicle parks
sections.summary: Most heavy vehicle lots are in industrial areas and privately operated, and public parks in or near residential areas are being progressively reduced while ensuring sufficient accessible lots.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Today, the majority of HV lots are already located in industrial areas and privately operated.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: As the Member has also pointed out, we have been reviewing our plans to progressively reduce the number of public HVPs in or near residential areas, to free up land to meet other development needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: HV drivers play an important role in our economy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: We are, therefore, working closely with agencies like MTI, MOT, ESG and LTA, to ensure that there remain sufficient HV lots islandwide which are accessible to drivers, as we phase out some of our public HVPs in or near residential areas.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: As part of this process, we take into consideration feedback from industry stakeholders, like HVP operators and HV-operating businesses, to address business needs and possible constraints.

sections.label: Agencies discussing with heavy vehicle businesses
sections.summary: Sector leads, Ministries and agencies are discussing these issues with their heavy vehicle operating businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Indeed, these are the issues that the various sector leads, the various Ministries and agencies, are discussing with their HV operating businesses.
